course_name_en: Religion, Meaning-making and Philosophy of Life
prerequisites: General knowledge of the main lines of philosophy, ethics and Western culture and history.

learning_outcomes.text: The student is able to clarify the role that philosophies of life and religions, especially the Christian faith tradition, play in culture and society.
To analyze which human and world views are present in phenomena in society and culture, such as media, healthcare, economy, technology, education, etc., and to be able to reflect critically on them.
To demonstrate and explain the uniqueness of philosophies of life and religions, especially the Christian faith tradition, using concrete examples.
To apply general theoretical views from theology and religious studies to current social themes.
To learn to recognize and critically deal with the religious and philosophical themes related to one's own field.
To develop and articulate a personal and well-founded vision on philosophical questions and phenomena, in dialogue with the Christian faith.
To name the value of religion, meaning-making, and faith attitudes in relation to aspects of one's own life ('philosophical thoughtfulness').
To integrate philosophical dimensions in the development of one's own professional identity.

syllabus_topics: The role of religions and the core of Christian faith in the context of other world religions
Contribution of faith to personal happiness
Christian expectation of the future in confrontation with humanist objections
Specificity of ethical commitment (norm erosion/norm shifting)
Relevance of a philosophy of life with regard to examples from engineering ethics
assessment_rules: The first exam opportunity is a multiple-choice exam, with approximately 20 percent of questions testing knowledge and 80 percent testing critical thinking. Resit and catch-up exams consist of three open questions.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
